key_insight: Universal machine-learning force fields make larger errors in multicomponent materials when local environments are underrepresented, highly heterogeneous, or compression-dominated.
engineering_relevance: For compositional design workflows, model choice and training-data coverage should be matched to the target chemistry and strain state to reduce force-field failure risk.
method: Built a benchmark of 7,599 multicomponent configurations inspired by high-entropy design, elemental substitution, and anion mixing.
Evaluated 11 pretrained models against DFT for energies, forces, stresses, and downstream elastic, vibrational, and adsorption-related properties.
Analyzed error drivers using training-reference distance, local geometry, directionality of interatomic separation, and elemental response patterns.
evidence_signal: Across the benchmark, force errors generally increased with distance from training-like environments, and after matching pair types and distance deviations, compression-side force errors were about 1.81–1.95× larger than extension-side errors.
watch_item: Coverage metrics help explain trends but do not fully predict error magnitude, so near-identical distances can still yield substantially different failures.
paper_title: Origins of Universal Machine Learning Force-Field Errors in Multicomponent Materials
